papers.text: A brass rail along every shop window, at nose height. The spotters know whose.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: The band would like the top of Gusting Heights. Then the sky over it. Kites, the rest.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A gold rosette for you at every national show. Cuthbert has entered you as an onion.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will pay to hang the timetable in every shop window. All of it. With footnotes.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Rename the hedge show the Hedge and Kite Show. Most of our kites are entered already.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Sound carries 40 % further over water. The band will pay to practise in rowing boats.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Let the Guild name the national bandstand this summer. Till's Teas has a suggestion.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A national inquiry into the word 'mild' in forecasts. The onions want it defined.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry has defined 'mild'. It now asks to look into 'fairly'.

papers.text: Clip the hedge by the kite field into a clock. It will be right to the nearest season.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: An inquiry into why kites land on buses. It will sit on the top deck.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry has outgrown the top deck. It asks for a second bus.

papers.text: Give the weigh-in the only dry Saturday. The kites can have the next one, in spring.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Kites rise 12 % better from a mown field. Mow the one beside the hedge show, please.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A desk fountain, with Lavinia's compliments. It gurgles whenever you are right.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the desk fountain: it has entered the hedge show, and would like to win.

clippings.sign: FOUNTAIN WINS HEDGE SHOW; HEDGES DAMP AND DISMAYED
clippings.refuse: FOUNTAIN SENT BACK. IT HAS NOT GURGLED SINCE

papers.text: The band took our Thursdays by the lake. Then our Fridays. We would like one back.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Ribbon offcuts for your desk. Just to practise on. Any openings coming up? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the offcuts: they would like a shop window for Window Week. The best one.

clippings.sign: OFFCUTS TAKE BEST WINDOW; GUILD DISPLAYS ITS DISMAY
clippings.refuse: OFFCUTS RETURNED UNCUT. MR SASH 'NOT UPSET'

papers.text: The League will pay to fly over the hedge show. Each kite to apply in writing.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A study of how far the tuba carries. First from the lake, then from the next lake along.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The tuba study asks to listen from a third lake, to be thorough.

papers.text: The Committee will pay for no wind on show day. Gwendolyn is getting a quote.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Sit in the Quiet Competition for an hour. Rodney asks if he may take a quiet photograph.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: The League would like to hire the wind over Brassby. They will pay.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Be photographed logging the 7:02, nose to a shop window, as is the custom.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An inquiry into where the wind goes after Gusting Heights. It will sit in the bandstand.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The wind inquiry has followed the wind to the lake. It asks for a boat.

papers.text: Signs round the lake that read SHH, and one on the bandstand that reads SHHH.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Say 'mild, with no wind' at the weigh-in. Onions do 3 % better when you say it.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: A barometer for your desk, from Consolidated Umbrellas. It only says RAIN.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the barometer: it would like the 7:02 held each morning until it has decided.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT HOLDS 7:02 FOR BAROMETER; SPOTTERS LOG DELAY
clippings.refuse: BAROMETER SENT BACK. IT SAW THIS COMING

papers.text: Move kite day away from the lake, please. Last year our floats took off.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Kites landed on the patch 12 times this year. One took second prize. A net, please.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A national inquiry into the shape of the wind. The Committee would like it squarer.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry could not find the wind's corners. It asks to look again in autumn.

papers.text: The spotters lean on our hedge, then their flasks, now a stepladder. Move the stop.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A launch ramp on Gusting Heights, please. The band is sitting on all the good wind.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: An inquiry into nose prints on shop windows. Witnesses will be asked to lean.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The nose-print inquiry asks for a second window. The first one is now evidence.

papers.text: Your speeches, bound in gilt. Mildred found them in the drawer FOR FURTHER STUDY.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Launch the first kite of the season, President. Let go when we say. Not before.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: The national bandstand, by the lake. Then a jetty for the tuba. Then a raft for the drum.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Have every forecast end with you, Rodney suggests. 'Mild, then the President.'
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Open the new pipe from the anglers' lake to the patch. Turn the tap slowly, for the camera.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: At the bus stop, kites now outnumber buses three to one. The stop is for buses.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A plaque for the draper's window: THE 7:02 WAS ON TIME HERE, ONCE.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Be photographed admiring Window Week. The best display covers the bus timetable.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: The Society will hire the bus shelters on show day. Onions only, one per seat.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
